name: Snare
description:
A leather strap pulled tight, which is stick-slip friction and nothing else: the cord grips, tears free, grips again, faster and tighter as the tension climbs. So there is no oscillator anywhere in this document. The first version had a filtered sawtooth sliding up underneath for body and it was the whole problem — a tone under a creak is a hum, and what came out was a low boom with some grit on top rather than a strap. Every voice here is noise cut into grains, and the sound is entirely in how those grains are spaced.

Three layers, and the shape is an acceleration. `grip` is the strap taking the strain: eight slow grains over thirteen hundredths, wide apart, in the low-mid band where leather has its body. `slip` arrives on top of it a tenth in with twice the grains in the same space and half the length each, bandpassed higher and with a sharp Q, which is the run of fast ticks the ear reads as *drrr* — and it is what the whole cue is named for. `bite` is three grains at the end, low and close together, where it stops moving. Nothing fades out: a strap that goes quiet has been let go, and this one is still tight when the sound ends.

The grains are jittered rather than evenly spaced, and that is load-bearing. Evenly spaced clicks are a ratchet, a ratchet is a machine, and there is no machinery anywhere in this game.
